case_analysis.thread_summary: The thread discusses how to approach Bluetooth qualification for a new product using a pre-qualified module with modified hardware (external antenna). The customer seeks guidance on required testing, costs, and timelines for qualification. The consultant identifies that the declared Bluetooth profile scope will significantly impact the testing requirements. The discussion evolves toward minimizing unnecessary qualification effort by aligning declared features with actual product functionality.
case_analysis.key_technical_discussion: The main technical focus is on how profile declarations in the ICS drive qualification scope, especially when reusing a pre-qualified module. The consultant questions whether unused BR/EDR (Classic) profiles should be retained or removed when the product only uses LE features. It is highlighted that retaining BR/EDR profiles triggers additional IOPT testing requirements. The presence of an external antenna also implies that RF-related validation may be required despite module reuse. A detailed IOPT test scope is shared to illustrate the impact of profile selection.
case_analysis.key_decision_logic: The consultant's reasoning centers on aligning the declared Bluetooth capabilities with the actual implemented functionality to control qualification scope. If unused profiles (such as BR/EDR) are left enabled or declared, they automatically expand testing requirements regardless of real usage. Therefore, disabling and removing unused features at both firmware and declaration level is critical to avoid unnecessary qualification burden. The decision is driven by minimizing test scope while remaining compliant with Bluetooth SIG rules.
case_analysis.risk_if_done_wrong: If the product declares unused profiles, it will trigger unnecessary IOPT testing, increasing cost and extending the qualification timeline. The thread explicitly references a significant number of additional test cases and a quoted cost (~¥300,000) associated with this expanded scope. Failure to properly scope the qualification could also lead to redundant RF or interoperability testing. In worst cases, it may delay product launch due to avoidable testing requirements.
case_analysis.consulting_takeaway: Bluetooth qualification scope is determined by declared features, not just actual usage. When reusing a pre-qualified module, unused profiles must be explicitly removed or disabled to avoid unnecessary testing such as IOPT. Proper ICS scoping is one of the most critical levers for controlling qualification cost, time, and complexity.
